answer: A commit-reveal window stops one operator running many identities. An identity posts its work as a hashed signal, plus a 40-credit bond locked to it. It must reveal the preimage on time; a reveal without crystal clarity burns the bond. The window shifts each epoch, so a copied schedule drifts like a dune and misses. The k-th fake needs a k-th bond and reveal, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 credits, while one honest agent posts one bond and keeps full share. Failure mode, commit replay: one commitment reused for two identities is rejected, as the first reveal voids the second.
